Project Proposal

Background and Problem Statement

The project topic will be based on VAST Challenge 2025. We have chosen Mini-Challenge 1.

VAST Challenge 2025 Mini Challenge 1 centres on the rise of Sailor Shift, a musician from the island nation of Oceanus. She’s famous for spreading the influence of the Oceanus Folk genre and frequently collaborating with lesser-known artists. Silas Reed, a local journalist, has assembled a knowledge graph encompassing artists, albums, songs, collaborations, and influence relationships spanning decades.

The challenge presents a rich but complex network dataset for us to uncover the structural patterns in how Sailor rose to fame, who she influenced, and how Oceanus Folk spread globally.

Our project aims to build a suite of coordinated Tableau dashboards that can transform this knowledge graph into a cohesive, interactive visual narrative — answering all prescribed analytical questions and going beyond to surface emergent insights about genre diffusion and the making of a music star.

Objectives

Our project is structured around three thematic clusters that map directly to the challenge tasks. We aim to explore and understand:

  1. Sailor Shift’s Career Profile
    • Who has she been most influenced by over time?
    • Who has she collaborated with and directly or indirectly influenced?
    • How has she influenced collaborators of the broader Oceanus Folk community?
  2. Spread of Oceanus Folk Genre
    • Was this influence intermittent or did it have a gradual rise?
    • What genres and top artists have been most influenced by Oceanus Folk?
    • On the converse, how has Oceanus Folk changed with the rise of Sailor Shift? From which genres does it draw most of its contemporary inspiration?
  3. Prediction and Profile of Rising Stars
    • Visualize the careers of three artists. Compare and contrast their rise in popularity and influence.
    • Using this characterization, give three predictions of who the next Oceanus Folk stars with be over the next five years.

Dataset Overview

The data provided by the challenge is a directed multigraph (MC1_graph.json) that contains 17,412 nodes and 27,857 edges spanning five node types and twelve relationship types.

The dataset was loaded using NetworkX’s node_link_graph() function in python. The description and schema of the data are categorised by nodes and edges:

Node Type Description Attributes
Person Anyone in the music industry, including singers, producers, instrumentalists, composers, etc name, stage_name (optional)
MusicalGroup Bands, quartets, small choirs, or other officially organized entities formed by musicians to make music name
RecordLabel Organizations—professional, commercial, or otherwise institutional—involved in the recording, production, or distribution of the music. name
Song Information on songs genre, release_date, notable (bool), notoriety_date (optional), single (optional), written_date (optional)
Album Information on albums genre, release_date, notable (bool), notoriety_date (optional), written_date (optional)
Edge Type Description
PerformerOf Indicates a that the source node (Person or MusicalGroup) performed the destination node (Song or Album)
ComposerOf Indicates that the source node (Person) composed the destination node (Song or Album)
ProducerOf Indicates that the source node (Person or RecordLabel) participated in the production of the destination node’s work (Song, Album, Person, or MusicalGroup)
LyricistOf Indicates that the source node (Person) wrote lyrics for the destination node (Song or Album)
RecordedBy Indicates that the destination node (RecordLabel) aided in the recording process for the source node (Song or Album)
DistributedBy Indicates that the destination node (RecordLabel) aided in the distribution process for the source node (Song or Album)
InStyleOf Indicates that the source node (Song or Album) was performed at least partly in the style of the destination node (Song, Album, Person, or MusicalGroup)
InterpolatesFrom Indicates that the source node (Song or Album) interpolated a melody from the destination node (Song or Album).
CoverOf Indicates that the source node (Song or Album) is a cover of the destination node (Song or Album)
LyricalReferenceTo Indicates that the source node (Song or Album) makes a lyrical reference to the destination node (Song or Album)
DirectlySamples Indicates that the source node (Song or Album) consists of (an) audio recording(s) that directly reuse a portion of the audio recording of the destination node (Song or Album) via sampling
MemberOf Indicates that the source node (Person) is (or was) a member of the destination node (MusicalGroup)

Proposed Methodology

The proposed data pipeline runs in three stages: (1) Python extraction and metric computation, (2) Gephi layout for network coordinates, and (3) Tableau ingestion and dashboard construction.

Data Preparation

Create a python file, parse_data.py, to extract csv files from the MC1_graph.json.

  1. Load the graph using NetworkX’s node_link_graph() to reconstruct the directed multigraph

    import json
import networkx as nx
import pandas as pd  

with open("MC1_graph.json", "r") as f:
    data = json.load(f)

G = nx.node_link_graph(data)

print(f"Nodes: {G.number_of_nodes()}")   # expect 17,412
print(f"Edges: {G.number_of_edges()}")   # expect 37,857

  2. Extract and split nodes into a dataframe

    
nodes = []
for node_id, attrs in G.nodes(data=True):
    row = {"id": node_id}
    row.update(attrs)
    nodes.append(row)

nodes_df = pd.DataFrame(nodes)
print(nodes_df["Node Type"].value_counts())

# Split into one table per node type
persons       = nodes_df[nodes_df["Node Type"] == "Person"].copy()
songs         = nodes_df[nodes_df["Node Type"] == "Song"].copy()
albums        = nodes_df[nodes_df["Node Type"] == "Album"].copy()
musical_groups= nodes_df[nodes_df["Node Type"] == "MusicalGroup"].copy()
record_labels = nodes_df[nodes_df["Node Type"] == "RecordLabel"].copy()

  3. Extract edges

    edges = []
for source, target, attrs in G.edges(data=True):
    row = {"source": source, "target": target}
    row.update(attrs)
    edges.append(row)

edges_df = pd.DataFrame(edges)
print(edges_df["Edge Type"].value_counts())

# Split into one table per edge type
performer_of       = edges_df[edges_df["Edge Type"] == "PerformerOf"]
composer_of        = edges_df[edges_df["Edge Type"] == "ComposerOf"]
producer_of        = edges_df[edges_df["Edge Type"] == "ProducerOf"]
lyricist_of        = edges_df[edges_df["Edge Type"] == "LyricistOf"]
recorded_by        = edges_df[edges_df["Edge Type"] == "RecordedBy"]
distributed_by     = edges_df[edges_df["Edge Type"] == "DistributedBy"]
member_of          = edges_df[edges_df["Edge Type"] == "MemberOf"]

# Influence-type edges
in_style_of        = edges_df[edges_df["Edge Type"] == "InStyleOf"]
interpolates_from  = edges_df[edges_df["Edge Type"] == "InterpolatesFrom"]
cover_of           = edges_df[edges_df["Edge Type"] == "CoverOf"]
lyrical_ref        = edges_df[edges_df["Edge Type"] == "LyricalReferenceTo"]
directly_samples   = edges_df[edges_df["Edge Type"] == "DirectlySamples"]

  4. Consolidate these edge types into a single influence table

    {python}
influence_edges = edges_df[edges_df["Edge Type"].isin([
    "InStyleOf", "InterpolatesFrom", "CoverOf",
    "LyricalReferenceTo", "DirectlySamples"
])].copy()

  5. Export nodes and edges into CSVs

    persons.to_csv("persons.csv", index=False)
songs.to_csv("songs.csv", index=False)
albums.to_csv("albums.csv", index=False)
musical_groups.to_csv("musical_groups.csv", index=False)
record_labels.to_csv("record_labels.csv", index=False)

influence_edges.to_csv("influence_edges.csv", index=False)
performer_of.to_csv("performer_of.csv", index=False)
composer_of.to_csv("composer_of.csv", index=False)
producer_of.to_csv("producer_of.csv", index=False)
member_of.to_csv("member_of.csv", index=False)

Gephi

  1. Import nodes and edges CSVs into Gephi
  2. Run ForceAtlas and adjust visual attributes to prepare graph visualisation
